newsitem.title: FRANCE: Algeria PM slams opposition on domestic policy.
newsitem.headline: Algeria PM slams opposition on domestic policy.

text.p: Algeria's Prime Minister Ahmed Ouyahia, who listened during four days to opposition parliament members hitting at his government over policy, on Wednesday slammed them over what he called their political backing of radical Islamists.
He urged all political parties to join in a united front to fight Moslem guerrillas locked with the Algerian government in a nearly six years of conflict in which more than 60,000 people have died.

The debate, broadcast live in Algerian television and shedding lights in issues previously seen as taboo -- like corruption, violence and justice -- gave the nation's 29 million people the first taste of plural political representation.
Algerians in June elected a 380-member National Assembly (lower house) made up of 10 political parties, including two Islamist-oriented groups, and 11 independents.
Ouyahia reminded his junior Islamist partners in the cabinet they are part of the government they were criticising.

"You have said 'government of liars'. You had two members in the previous cabinet and seven positions in the current one," Ouyahia told a deputy in the house from Islamist-based Movement of a Peaceful Society (MPS).
MPS deputies have joined opposition deputies to criticise parts of the government programme being debated in the house ahead of a vote of confidence scheduled for next Saturday.

Ouyahia bitterly hit at secular opposition parties, the Socialist Forces Front (FFS) and left-wing Workers Party (PT), over their positions calling for a dialogue with radical Islamists to try to end violence.

"You are now weeping for the victims of terrorism while you are using the term 'militiamen' for those Algerians who have taken up weapons to defend their lives, their families and help in defending Algeria," he said.
He reminded the FFS and PT of what he called their efforts abroad to lobby foreign countries to impose an embargo against Algeria with the aim of putting pressure on their leaders to end violence.
"You are crying out that people are hungry and (yet) you have sought to clamp an embargo on Algeria," he said.
But he urged all political forces to work together to forge a front against "terrorism" and cooperate to further democracy and economic reforms.

The government has a majority to secure enough votes in the house to pass its three-year programme which included creating 1.2 million jobs, building 800,000 housing units and buttressing gross domestic product to seven percent by year from an average 4 percent in the past two years.
